## Source map and comparison

The library is a catalog and tool execution layer, not a complete hypothesis workflow. Its central [`ToolUniverse` runtime](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L336-L376) loads selected tools and dispatches sync/async invocations. Tool descriptions/configuration and separate `skills/` workflows are its prompt-facing surface; they do not replace our specialist prompts or graph.

| Concern | Shipped source and evidence | Comparison question |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | [Registry](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_registry.py#L58-L146) combines decorated/configured tools, a generated lazy map, AST fallback and plugin entry points. [Compact MCP mode](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/guide/building_ai_scientists/compact_mode.rst#L6-L54) exposes list/grep/info/execute rather than sending the entire catalog to the model. | Does current tool selection already bound context, and would progressive disclosure improve a demonstrated lookup? |
| Finder | [Keyword discovery](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_keyword.py#L726-L791) uses TF-IDF; [embedding](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_embedding.py#L258-L280) and [LLM](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_llm.py#L442-L490) finders are separate optional paths. | Can deterministic discovery help without paid embeddings or an additional LLM route? |
| Parameter validation | [`BaseTool.validate_parameters`](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_tool.py#L340-L477) checks JSON Schema and gives unknown-key/typo guidance. | Does the existing MCP/engine boundary give equally actionable errors without revealing sensitive inputs? |
| Error envelope | [Error types](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/exceptions.py#L8-L36) carry class, retryability and suggested next steps; the [runtime envelope](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L4452-L4458) retains `status`, `error`, `error_details`. | Could a failure guide an agent's retry while preserving provenance and security? |
| Result cache | [Two-tier manager](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/cache/result_cache_manager.py#L47-L81) uses memory/SQLite, TTL, versioned namespace and singleflight; a [tool run opts in](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L2982-L3010). | Are current evidence retrieval caches provenance-safe, and is any added cache worth its invalidation cost? |
| Composition | [Compose functions](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L18-L89) invoke other registered tools and auto-load regex-discovered dependencies; [degradation handling](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L313-L333) can annotate missing dependencies. | Does our existing multi-source literature search need any of this, or would importing a second composition runtime bypass evidence and cost controls? |
| Connector adapters | [REST](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_rest_tool.py#L22), [GraphQL](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/graphql_tool.py#L128), and [MCP](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py#L275) sit beside provider-specific Python connectors and local-model configs. A [catalog-integrity test](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_compose_tool_dependencies.py#L58-L75) counts more than 1,000 names; that is catalog breadth, not 1,000 live-validated services. | Which individual connector fills a real scientific gap after checking our existing catalog, provider terms and live availability? |

The [tool-discovery agent configuration](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/data/tool_discovery_agents.json#L3-L47) supplies prompt-driven tool generation. It is not required to expose a selected connector through our existing MCP runtime. Inline [composition execution](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L422-L450) invokes `exec` on configured code; importing it would add a separate trusted-code execution path outside the current confinement boundary, so this campaign will assess the composition idea without running or adopting that path.

## Tests and operational assumptions

[Upstream unit tests](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_cache_manager.py#L11-L47) exercise cache TTL and restart; [composition tests](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_compose_tool_dependencies.py#L58-L75) cover dependency declarations, and an [MCP integration suite](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/integration/test_mcp_protocol.py) covers the protocol. The pinned [pytest configuration](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/pytest.ini#L1-L10) excludes network, API-key and slow tests by default, so shipped tests do not prove every connector works live or produces valid scientific evidence. None has been executed in this campaign checkout.

The [MCP server](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/smcp_server.py#L789-L794) defaults to loopback and requires a bearer-token environment variable for non-loopback binding. [Request-scoped credentials](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/guide/api_keys.rst#L14-L53) are documented as cache-disabled and instance-partitioned. Calls can transmit arguments to [more than 200 providers](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/PRIVACY.md#L25-L35); some consume [account credits](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/data/api_keys_catalog.json#L293-L300), and the optional embedding finder downloads model weights. Their service/privacy terms and billing paths must be verified per selected connector. No upstream agent setup, broad install, ambient-key experiment or paid service is authorized.

## Fidelity boundary

Google's public product description calls for a grounded knowledge base whose ideas link to verified scientific references, and the paper describes literature-informed specialist agents ([local source extraction](../../docs/FIDELITY.md)). It does not prescribe ToolUniverse's catalog size, protocol, cache design or connector roster. Every ToolUniverse finding is therefore an **external technique** until separately justified by an observed local gap; connector choice and adapter shape are **local design choices**. A new tool must preserve our source IDs, claim/evidence lineage, safety gate and zero-cost routing rather than implying that its presence makes an idea scientifically validated.
